extracted.intended_audience: utilities (pole owners), attachers (broadband providers/telecoms), and legal/policy practitioners engaged in FCC pole-attachment proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and adopted rules governing what pole-related information utilities must (or need not) provide to prospective attachers, how amendments affect review periods, and the Commission's balancing of disclosure benefits against utility burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide inspection-report information upon application request
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilities will be required to furnish already available information in pole inspection reports concerning specific poles upon request at the time an attachment application is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule ties requests for information to poles contained in submitted attachment applications and covers information utilities already collect in the normal course of inspections (e.g., which poles have been identified as needing replacement). The Commission declines to require broader duties beyond inspection-report data at this time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not require utilities to gather or provide extensive pole-related data beyond ordinary inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilities should not be required by rule to gather and provide extensive pole-related data for every pole attachment application about matters they do not track in the normal course of business through their inspections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record shows many utilities do not create schedules or databases for every pole; imposing such duties would be burdensome and costly. The Commission declines to codify broad new data-collection obligations that utilities do not already maintain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to restart 45-day review period on amended applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the new rule, utilities will always have the option of electing to restart the 45-day review period when an applicant amends an application; utilities are required to actually review an amended application to determine whether a restart is necessary given the specific circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission rejected proposals to automatically restart or force filing of new applications when amendments occur; instead, utilities must assess whether an amendment is 'minor' or necessitates a restart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not codify a pre-application duty to provide pole information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission declines to require utilities to provide attachers with pole information prior to the attacher submitting a pole attachment application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-application duties would require a new process/timeline prior to the make-ready process and are unnecessary because attachers can obtain information via pre-application surveys and visual inspection; however, the Commission 'strongly encourage[s]' voluntary pre-application collaboration and information sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage voluntary information sharing without disincentivizing it
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission stresses that adopting a requirement to provide inspection reports but not codifying additional mandates should not be read to undermine or disincentivize voluntary pre-application sharing by utilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntary sharing promotes transparency and can reduce make-ready costs, disputes, and delays. The Commission will monitor whether voluntary arrangements sufficiently promote broadband deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitive/critical infrastructure information protections remain
rubrics_metrics.description: The new rule is not intended to override laws precluding disclosure of certain critical infrastructure information; legal constraints can be addressed via appropriate redactions or non-disclosure agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters noted security/homeland-security concerns; parties may use confidentiality agreements or redact legitimately protected information. Utilities should work in good faith to provide what they can without violating other laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decline to require creation of utility pole-information databases or a single national database
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission declines to require each utility to create an accessible database with an array of data on all its poles or to establish a single pole-information database for all utilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons: burdens and costs of creating/updating a database for potentially millions of poles are very large; information would likely be out of date; benefits are speculative and are reduced by the adopted inspection-report disclosure requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer surveys (attacher pre-application survey or utility make-ready survey) for up-to-date pole info
rubrics_metrics.description: A pre-application survey conducted by the attacher, or a make-ready survey conducted by a utility in response to a specific attachment application, are often the best ways to ensure up-to-date, accurate information on the current state of poles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual inspection may reveal age, red-tags, latest inspection date, load and suitability; attachers are free to retain contractors to map/survey poles at their cost rather than imposing timelines/costs on utilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: No mandatory requirement to provide loading studies (but provide if in inspection reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent pole inspection reports include loading studies, attachers will have access under the new rule; the Commission declines to adopt a requirement that utilities provide loading studies in other cases or to dictate when a utility can require a loading study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission strongly encourages utilities to provide loading studies when reasonably requested and readily available, and recognizes loading studies can be important for safety, reliability, and engineering concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject mandatory disclosure of pole age, height, class, and condition (unless in inspection reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission rejects attachers' requests to require utilities to provide data on the age, height, class, and condition of poles, or the last inspection/make-ready/fix dates, beyond what is contained in inspection reports or routinely provided in the application process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utilities state such information is often provided in make-ready estimates, visible on poles during inspection (e.g., installation year, red tags), or not tracked. The Commission 'strongly encourage[s]' utilities to share readily available information collected in the normal course of business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decline to require disclosure of broad operational/financial records beyond existing rule disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests that utilities be required to provide extensive operational or financial data (e.g., replacement schedules, outside plant records, detailed accounting records, financial records regarding pole-related charges, data to rebut presumptions in rate calculations) are denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some financial information is already required to be disclosed under existing rules; the Commission will not adopt new sweeping disclosure requirements because of cost/burden and limited marginal benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid imposing broad disclosure requirements that force utilities to expend significant resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Codifying a broad disclosure requirement for all information collected in the ordinary course of business could force utilities to expend significant resources to gather such information and could lead to additional disputes and complaints related to information sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission encourages voluntary sharing but rejects mandatory, broad reporting/retention requirements that would be costly and may slow deployment.
